title: Competing Interlayer Loop Currents and Superconductivity in the Bilayer $t$-$J_\perp$-$V$ Model
authors: Luciano Zinni, Fabricio Gómez, Jun Zhan, Matías Bejas, Xianxin Wu, Andreas P. Schnyder, Andrés Greco
abstract: The recent discovery of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in pressurized and thin-film bilayer nickelates, featuring a strong interlayer exchange coupling, and their potential similarities with cuprate superconductors, has made this a very active topic in condensed matter physics. In the present paper we study the strongly correlated one-orbital ($d_{x^2-y^2}$) bilayer $t$-$J_\perp$-$V$ model for nickelates, where $V$ denotes the Coulomb interactions, using a controlled large-$N$ expansion at and beyond the mean-field level. Focusing on the out-of-plane spin exchange interaction ($J_\perp$), we find that it triggers both out-of-plane $s$-wave superconductivity and an out-of-plane bond-order phase ($z$-BOP) instability. The $z$-BOP gives rise to a complex $z$-axis hopping dominated by its imaginary component, which drives out-of-plane currents and induces in-plane ones, spontaneously forming on the vertical plaquettes a loop-current state that breaks time-reversal symmetry. Competition between this loop-current phase and superconductivity yields a dome-shaped superconducting region, with optimal superconductivity occurring near the $z$-BOP quantum critical point. The resulting phase diagram features a pure loop-current region, a low-doping coexistence phase, a pure superconducting state at higher doping, and a correlated metallic state.
summary: This theoretical study models high-Tc superconductivity in bilayer nickelates using the $t$-$J_{\perp}$-$V$ model. It finds that an out-of-plane bond-order phase instability generates loop currents that compete with superconductivity. This competition results in a characteristic dome-shaped superconducting phase diagram, suggesting a quantum critical point governs optimal pairing.
main_problem: The paper investigates the competition between out-of-plane loop currents (LCs) and superconductivity (SC) in bilayer nickelates, a system relevant to high-Tc superconductivity.
main_result: The out-of-plane bond-order phase ($z$-BOP) instability drives the formation of time-reversal symmetry breaking loop currents, leading to a dome-shaped superconducting region optimal near the $z$-BOP quantum critical point.
method: The study employs a controlled large-$N$ expansion, analyzing the self-consistent gap equations for both the superconducting gap ($\Delta_\perp$) and the complex $z$-BOP gap ($\phi$).
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the strongly correlated one-orbital ($	ext{d}_{x^2-y^2}$) bilayer $t$-$J_{\perp}$-$V$ model for nickelates. The Hamiltonian includes hopping, spin exchange ($J_{\perp}$), and Coulomb interactions ($V$).
key_observables: Superconducting gap ($\Delta_\perp$), $z$-BOP gaps ($\phi_{r\perp}, \phi_{A\perp}$), induced in-plane currents, orbital magnetic moment, and the phase diagram structure.
important_parameters: Doping ($\delta$), interlayer exchange coupling ($J_{\perp}$), and the ratio of hopping parameters ($t_{\perp}/t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the $z$-BOP gap is purely imaginary ($\phi = i \phi_{A\perp}$), and that Coulomb interactions are less critical than the spin/hopping terms for the primary instabilities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the real and imaginary $z$-BOP gaps versus doping, showing the dominance of the imaginary component ($\phi_{A\perp}$), and map out the phase diagram showing LC, SC, and coexisting regions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the coupled gap equations for SC and $z$-BOP order parameters, analyzes the resulting magnetic flux and current patterns, and maps the resulting phase diagram as a function of doping.
why_interesting: The explicit theoretical modeling of competing orders (charge/orbital vs. superconducting) in a strongly correlated lattice model provides a rich playground for understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms, which is a major focus in condensed matter theory.
